books.title: Strong Like You
books.author: T. L. Simpson
books.ratingNote: Goodreads ratings trend positive among readers of rural, sports-centered YA.
reviewSummary: Readers describe this as a quiet but emotionally heavy story about grief, masculinity, and loyalty. Many praise the restrained writing and the way it captures a boy searching for his missing father without turning sentimental. Often called short, tense, and deeply affecting.

books.title: Cope Field
books.author: T. L. Simpson
books.ratingNote: Early Goodreads reviews highlight character depth and emotional realism.
reviewSummary: A story about anger, silence, and learning to speak honestly in a family shaped by fame. Readers praise the slow-burn romance and the emotional weight beneath Craw’s restraint. Frequently described as grounded and quietly powerful.

books.title: The Way I Am Now
books.author: Amber Smith
books.ratingNote: Goodreads readers strongly engage with its trauma-recovery focus.
reviewSummary: A continuation of Eden’s story as her assault case goes to trial. Readers praise the honesty around healing not being linear and the emotional realism of justice moving slowly. Often described as validating but heavy.

books.title: The Way I Used to Be
books.author: Amber Smith
books.ratingNote: Widely read with sustained discussion and classroom use.
reviewSummary: A raw portrayal of how sexual assault reshapes identity across four years of high school. Readers call it painful but necessary, praising its refusal to soften reality or rush healing.

books.title: Field Notes on Love
books.author: Jennifer E. Smith
books.ratingNote: Goodreads readers praise its warmth and romantic tone.
reviewSummary: A cross-country train romance built on missed chances and new beginnings. Readers describe it as cozy, reflective, and gently hopeful, with strong chemistry and emotional payoff.

books.title: The Last to Let Go
books.author: Amber Smith
books.ratingNote: Consistently strong ratings from readers of emotionally heavy YA.
reviewSummary: A story about siblings left on their own after a family tragedy. Readers praise its exploration of guilt, freedom, and resilience. Often described as heartbreaking but hopeful.

books.title: Don't Read the Comments
books.author: Eric Smith
books.ratingNote: Goodreads ratings are especially strong among gamer teens.
reviewSummary: A tense look at online harassment, fame, and digital identity. Readers praise its realism around doxxing and misogyny, calling it timely and unsettling.

books.title: See You Yesterday
books.author: Rachel Lynn Solomon
books.ratingNote: Highly rated for humor and time-loop premise.
reviewSummary: A rom-com-style time loop set on the first day of college. Readers love the banter, physics jokes, and gradual romance.

books.title: Past Present Future
books.author: Rachel Lynn Solomon
books.ratingNote: Positive Goodreads response from fans of realistic romance.
reviewSummary: A long-distance relationship tested by college life. Readers praise its emotional maturity and honesty about change.

books.title: You'll Miss Me When I'm Gone
books.author: Rachel Lynn Solomon
books.ratingNote: Highly rated for emotional depth and representation.
reviewSummary: Twin sisters face love, faith, and a devastating genetic test. Readers describe it as heartbreaking and beautifully written.

books.title: An Echo in the City
books.author: K. X. Song
books.ratingNote: Praised for political relevance and emotional realism.
reviewSummary: A coming-of-age love story set during the Hong Kong protests. Readers highlight the tension between activism and personal safety.

books.title: On the Bright Side
books.author: Anna Sortino
books.ratingNote: Strong praise for disability representation.
reviewSummary: A tender romance about Deaf identity, illness, and community. Readers call it hopeful, romantic, and deeply human.

books.title: Give Me a Sign
books.author: Anna Sortino
books.ratingNote: Popular among readers seeking Deaf representation.
reviewSummary: A joyful summer-camp romance celebrating Deaf pride and self-acceptance. Often described as warm and affirming.

books.title: Rabbit and Juliet
books.author: Rebecca Stafford
books.ratingNote: Early Goodreads reviews praise intensity and feminist anger.
reviewSummary: A dark, raw novel about grief, queer love, and revenge. Readers describe it as furious, unsettling, and cathartic.

books.title: The Gravity of Us
books.author: Phil Stamper
books.ratingNote: Goodreads readers praise its romance and media critique.
reviewSummary: A NASA-adjacent romance exploring fame, ethics, and first love under public pressure.

books.title: When My Heart Joins the Thousand
books.author: A. J. Steiger
books.ratingNote: Well-regarded for neurodivergent representation.
reviewSummary: A fragile, intense love story between two teens navigating illness and trauma.

books.title: The Exact Opposite of Okay
books.author: Laura Steven
books.ratingNote: Highly praised for humor and feminist themes.
reviewSummary: A sharp, funny story about slut-shaming, media outrage, and reclaiming identity.

books.title: Dress Codes for Small Towns
books.author: Courtney Stevens
books.ratingNote: Beloved for its exploration of sexual fluidity.
reviewSummary: A small-town story about friendship, labels, and love outside binaries.

books.title: Every Borrowed Beat
books.author: Erin Stewart
books.ratingNote: Early Goodreads reviews trend emotionally positive.
reviewSummary: A tender exploration of love, illness, and borrowed time.

books.title: Dust
books.author: Alison Stine
books.ratingNote: Praised for climate-fiction realism.
reviewSummary: A near-future climate story centered on disability, survival, and connection.

books.title: Arden Grey
books.author: Ray Stoeve
books.ratingNote: Strong praise for queer and ace representation.
reviewSummary: An emotionally honest story about toxic relationships and learning what healthy love looks like.

books.title: Dear Martin
books.author: Nic Stone
books.ratingNote: Goodreads ratings remain strong with classroom discussion use.
reviewSummary: A letter-based novel examining racism, privilege, and moral responsibility. Readers praise its urgency and clarity.

books.title: Dear Manny
books.author: Nic Stone
books.ratingNote: Positive early ratings following the Dear Martin series.
reviewSummary: A college-set continuation exploring activism, privilege, and political love.

books.title: Jo & Laurie
books.author: Melissa de la Cruz, Margaret Stohl
books.ratingNote: Goodreads response mixed but engaged among classics fans.
reviewSummary: A reimagining of Little Women focused on adulthood, ambition, and unresolved love.

books.title: Chaos Theory
books.author: Nic Stone
books.ratingNote: Readers praise mental health representation.
reviewSummary: A romance centered on grief, addiction, and learning self-worth.

books.title: Little Do We Know
books.author: Tamara Ireland Stone
books.ratingNote: Steady Goodreads engagement over time.
reviewSummary: A layered story about faith, friendship, and secrets that change everything.

books.title: Dear Justyce
books.author: Nic Stone
books.ratingNote: Highly praised for justice-system realism.
reviewSummary: Letters from an incarcerated teen expose systemic injustice and moral complexity.

books.title: Cool. Awkward. Black.
books.author: Karen Strong (Editor)
books.ratingNote: Strong anthology ratings driven by representation.
reviewSummary: A multi-genre collection celebrating Black geek culture in all its forms.

books.title: I Am Not Alone
books.author: Francisco X. Stork
books.ratingNote: Goodreads readers praise its social relevance.
reviewSummary: A tense story about immigration, justice, and friendship under pressure.
